q: In a frenzy of panic, we decided to explore all possibilities to hire a jhapa at the earliest.
cx: Their booked postpartum carer pulled out a month before the due date, so they rushed to hire one through agencies in India.

q: In one instance, we interviewed a candidate at 7:30 PM and informed the agency that we are good to go ahead by 11:30 PM. We were informed that another family had already booked the jhapa.
cx: How fast live-in mother-and-baby carers in India get booked by other families.

q: Jhapa for Mother-Baby Care - 35KService Charge of Agency - 5.5K + GST (Once finalised, searching fees is adjusted in this) - This charge is for a 3 month contract.
cx: One agency's rupee pricing for a three-month live-in postpartum carer; the agency the author would choose again.

q: I’ve seen so many different products, like ice pads, padsicles, witch hazel pads, disposable underwear and maternity pads, and they can get quite expensive. I don’t want to buy lots of things that I won’t actually use!
cx: UK poster packing for after the birth, unsure which postpartum care products are worth buying.

q: None of this was individually expensive, which I think is exactly how they got me.
cx: At 31 weeks she opens a drawer full of baby gadgets she bought after social-media 'essentials' videos.

q: Pregnancy has apparently turned me into the easiest marketing demographic on earth. Put "new mom must-have" in front of something and my brain immediately goes, well shit, what if I need it at 3am and don't have it?
cx: Why she kept buying baby gadgets: fear of being caught unprepared at night.

q: Then another person would say the first product was useless but THIS slightly different product saved their sanity, so obviously I'd start researching that too.
cx: The loop of conflicting product recommendations online during pregnancy.

q: My SIL loved having a owlet sock for her two kids and highly recommended it to my husband and I. It is a bit pricey, so we decided to splurge and buy it during the Labor Day sale.
cx: Bought a pricey baby monitor sock on a relative's recommendation; now weighing a return before the window closes.

q: After taking a childhood safety class at our hospital, the nurses stated that Owlet socks are not AAP recommended.
cx: A hospital class contradicted the relative's product recommendation.

q: My boyfriend really wants me to give birth privately in an NHS hospital like the Lindo Wing to avoid neglect or significant trauma.
cx: UK first-time mother; her partner pushes for a private maternity wing because of NHS maternity headlines.

q: My cousin really put me off the NHS postnatal wards saying they’re a sauna and you share with multiple other women, some who are quite unwell.
cx: A relative's account of NHS postnatal wards that made her consider paying for a private room.

q: You give birth under the NHS and then go to the Westminster Maternity Suite within their private wing, it’s around £1050.
cx: The private postnatal-room option she found at a London hospital and its price.

q: Interesting thank you, so many options and I’m finding it quite difficult to understand some of them tbh. Even within private care, you can have a lot of options.
cx: Confused by the different private maternity options in the UK.

q: A lot of comments were kinda assumptions about private care rather than actual experiences / not quite matching what I’m reading on their website
cx: She distrusts second-hand opinions about private care and wants real experiences.

q: Third pregnancy and using insurance this time around to get wearable pumps. There are way more options than there used to be.
cx: Third-time mother choosing among the $0-40 insurance-covered wearable pumps after buying her own before.

q: I’m looking for an alternative to a $350 3-hour-per-week in-person hypnobirthing class, preferably something self paced and less than $100.
cx: Pregnant with her second, preparing for a birth-centre birth without epidural on a tight budget.

q: With my last baby I tried to prepare for an un-medicated birth, but everywhere I looked I got hit by paywalls and super aggressive/predatory marketing (”I have the secret to a pain-free birth, but only if you pay me a bunch of money. Otherwise you’re doomed to suffer!”).
cx: How birth-preparation marketing felt to her the first time.

q: In the end I watched a few videos and read about half of the Mongan-method hypnobirthing book and Ina May‘s Guide to Childbirth, but when it actually came to the labor I expended way too much energy in early labor and ended up getting an epidural cause I was just so dang exhausted.
cx: What she did to prepare for her first birth, and why she thinks it fell short.

q: I feel like I need to do a lot more preparation if I’m going to be successful in that.
cx: Second time round she wants more structured preparation for an unmedicated birth.

q: they meet five times from 6:00-9:00 pm which is going to be really hard to work into my schedule. The class fee if also $350 which is a lot for my budget right now.
cx: Why the midwife-recommended local hypnobirthing class doesn't work for her.

q: I just get so bogged down when I try to google anything. There are so many ads and it leaves a bad taste in my mouth. (I have a whole rant about why is everyone trying to monetize birth and shouldn’t this just be common knowledge by now, but I’ll spare you all).
cx: Her resentment of paid birth-preparation ads while searching for a course.

q: I was just looking at the gentle birth app. Did you feel like it offered you enough structure to know what to do and how to practice?
cx: What she wants from a cheap self-paced option: structure and a practice plan.

q: I’m 30 weeks pregnant right now and my husband really wants to hire a night nurse. The money (thankfully) isnt an issue just wondering if it will be beneficial.
cx: Her husband wants a night nurse though both will be home; she is unsure it's needed.

q: Do you feel like I will miss out on any bonding time with the baby?
cx: Her worry about hiring overnight help for the newborn weeks.

q: In my mind, they were expensive, bulky, unnecessary, and would take over my bed and leave my poor husband hanging off the side.
cx: Her reasons for resisting a full-body pregnancy pillow before she gave in.

q: Well, at 19 weeks, after getting less and less sleep each night, waking up every hour and having trouble falling back asleep, I finally bought the stupid pillow. Last night I slept 8.5 hours!!!
cx: After weeks of poor sleep she bought a large pregnancy pillow and slept through.

q: It feels like clothing designers forgot that petite women also get pregnant sometimes and need pants to fit them during this chapter of their lives.  I’m 5’2 and 8 weeks pregnant with my second.
cx: Already outgrowing regular trousers early in her second pregnancy.

q: Is anyone else having to pay for everything out of pocket? How are you handling that?
cx: US mother pregnant without insurance, over the income limit for state help.

q: My last pregnancy was smooth, but anything can happen with this now especially now that I’m a little older. I don’t know what we would do if I needed to stay in the hospital for an extended period of time
cx: Uninsured in her second pregnancy, she fears the cost of a long hospital stay.

q: I had insurance through my husband’s job but our premiums went up so much we had to take me off but was able to afford living our son on.
cx: How she ended up pregnant without coverage in the US.

q: When I was pregnant, I looked into & considered so many things for baby but never once looked into investing in care from a lactation consultant. I never was told how difficult it could be & just assumed BF was a natural & easy thing for mom/baby to do
cx: Five weeks postpartum, a first-time mother wishes she had booked lactation help before the birth.

q: The 2-3 days in the hospital is not at all enough to see how your breasts, nipples, baby, and overall breastfeeding would change once home by yourself.
cx: Why hospital lactation visits weren't enough for her.

q: Theres nothing worse than being up at 4 am completely exhausted & tearful, looking up how-to youtube videos, with a red face crying baby who isn’t latching & pushing away from you, while your nipples are cracked & bleeding.
cx: The early-newborn night scene she wants others to avoid.

q: So when you get the estimate, screenshot or PDF the page and hold onto it somewhere accessible. I got a bill for a small copay about 10 weeks after the test was run
cx: A prenatal-test lab dropped a surprise copay after she showed the saved cost estimate.

q: I need a literal step by step guide of what is a must have for my baby, does that exist anywhere?
cx: At 17 weeks with her first, she has bought almost nothing and wants a plain list.

q: how do people afford to spend 200-800 dollars on each “bigger” item? I quite frankly can’t wrap my mind around how my fiance and I are going to afford that.
cx: The cost of big baby items worries her and her fiance.

q: Quite frankly all we have are gifts from others and it’s like 4 onesies and a stuffed animal.
cx: What she has ready for the baby at 17 weeks.

q: No one has bought a single thing 😐 not even the people who specifically asked for the link. I'm 34 weeks now.
cx: Second baby ten years after the first; nobody has bought from her registry.

q: No one checks in to see how I'm doing. No one asks about the baby. I'm trying not to take it personally and maybe I'm just in my feelings tonight but it genuinely feels like no one cares.
cx: How a second pregnancy feels ignored by family and friends.

q: It just sucks that everyone was so excited about my first and spoiled her so much but can't even take 30 seconds to ask about this baby :/ literally had a family member say "oh yeah I forgot you were pregnant" the other day
cx: What a relative said to her late in her second pregnancy.

q: for the first few years after my first was born EVERYONE would ask "so when you having another one?" "about time for a brother or sister huh?". It's like I didn't get pregnant again within the time frame they found appropriate so they just forgot about us.
cx: The contrast between pressure for a second child and silence once she was pregnant.

q: I’ve done my hypnobirthing course, read all the books on physiological birth…. Only to now be “overdue” and unable to relax because the overdue label and all the appointments and conversations are stressing me out!
cx: Past her due date, the preparation itself makes her anxious about not relaxing enough.

q: I’m feeling a lot of pressure to relax while being completely unable to.
cx: Past due date after a hypnobirthing course.

q: I am in desperate need to hear stories of people who went into labor while not in a perfectly relaxed state. Is there any hope here?? 🥲
cx: What she asks strangers while waiting past her due date.

q: Basically my beloved bugaboo donkey pram is just too big and heavy for me to get in and out of the car on my own now im in the second trimester
cx: Pregnant with a baby nearly one; she swapped to a £50 second-hand stroller she can lift.

q: I only paid £50 for the woosh 3 and it comes with the footmuff, cup holder and raincover so it feels like a good bargain
cx: Second-hand lightweight stroller bought for outings alone with her baby while pregnant.
